title: Astronomy: The Solar System
description: Planets, moons and the Sun: a tour of our corner of the Milky Way

questions.question: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.explanation: Mercury orbits closest to the Sun, at an average distance of about 58 million km.

questions.question: Which is the largest planet in the Solar System?
questions.explanation: Jupiter is the largest planet; its mass is more than twice that of all the other planets combined.

questions.question: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.explanation: Mars looks red because iron oxide (rust) in its dust and rocks colors its surface.

questions.question: Which planet has the hottest average surface temperature?
questions.explanation: Venus is hotter than Mercury despite being farther from the Sun: its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat, keeping the surface around 465 °C.

questions.question: Roughly how long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
questions.explanation: Earth sits about 150 million km from the Sun, so light moving at about 300,000 km/s takes roughly 8 minutes 20 seconds to arrive.

questions.question: What is the name of the band of rocky bodies between Mars and Jupiter?
questions.explanation: The main Asteroid Belt lies between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter. The Kuiper Belt is much farther out, beyond Neptune.

questions.question: In 2006 the International Astronomical Union reclassified Pluto as what?
questions.explanation: The IAU's 2006 definition requires a planet to have cleared its orbital neighborhood. Pluto has not, so it became a dwarf planet.

questions.question: What is the largest moon in the Solar System?
questions.explanation: Jupiter's moon Ganymede is the largest moon, and is even bigger than the planet Mercury. Saturn's Titan is a close second.

questions.question: Which planet rotates on its side, with an axial tilt of about 98 degrees?
questions.explanation: Uranus is tipped over so far that it effectively rolls along its orbit, likely the result of a giant collision long ago.

questions.question: What type of star is the Sun?
questions.explanation: The Sun is a G-type main-sequence star, often called a yellow dwarf. It fuses hydrogen into helium in its core.
